title: Separatedness of a separated scheme etale chart and its pullbacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $U$ be an $S$-scheme that is separated as a scheme (absolutely). If $u:h_U\to E$ is a representable etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], then $u$ is separated in the representable sense: its diagonal is a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every scheme $C$ over $S$ with a morphism $c:h_C\to E$, the scheme fibre product $C\times_EU\to C$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 03FZ (spaces-properties, lemma-separated-cover), with the base-change permanence of separated morphisms (Morphisms Tag 01UA).

proof.text: Write $a:U\to S$ for the structure morphism. Absolute separatedness says that $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] to $U\xrightarrow{a}S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: $a$ is separated, so its diagonal $\delta:U\to P:=U\times_SU$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No separatedness of $S$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03FZ (lemma-separated-cover), proof: U to S is separated; Schemes Tag 01KV (lemma-compose-after-separated)

proof.text: By representability in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $R:=U\times_EU$ is a scheme, with its natural map $j:R\to P$ and diagonal $d:U\to R$. The square with top $d:U\to R$, bottom $\delta:U\to P$, left $\mathrm{id}_U$, and right $j$ is cartesian. Indeed, for a test $S$-scheme $T$, an element of $R(T)$ is a pair $(x,y)$ of maps $T\to U$ with $u(x)=u(y)$. An element of $U\times_PR$ is therefore a triple $(z,x,y)$ with $(z,z)=(x,y)$; it is uniquely $(z,z,z)$, since $u(z)=u(z)$ imposes no further condition. The maps $z\mapsto(z,z,z)$ and $(z,x,y)\mapsto z$ are mutually inverse and commute with restriction in $T$. This is precisely the fibre-product universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 03FZ (lemma-separated-cover), diagonal argument expanded directly using its scheme R and map j

proof.text: By the cartesian square in step 2, $d$ is the base change of the closed immersion $\delta$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] shows that $d$ is a closed immersion. Applying the same lemma to $d$ and any scheme map $T\to R$ shows that every scheme base change of the diagonal of $u$ is a closed immersion, which is the asserted representable separatedness.

Fix $c:h_C\to E$ and let $W=C\times_EU$. This is a scheme because $u$ is representable [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The map $k:W\times_CW\to R$ sends $((t,x),(t,y))$ to $(x,y)$. The square with top $W\to U$ the second projection, bottom $k:W\times_CW\to R$, left $\Delta_{W/C}$, and right $d$ is cartesian: its test-object data are $t:T\to C$ and $x,y:T\to U$ with $c(t)=u(x)=u(y)$, together with $z:T\to U$ satisfying $x=z=y$; these are uniquely the data $(t,z)$ of $W(T)$. Thus $\Delta_{W/C}$ is a base change of $d$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], and is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $W\to C$ is separated.

lean.statement: theorem separated_etale_chart {S : Scheme.{u}} (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : Over S) [Scheme.IsSeparated U.left] (u : yoneda.obj U ⟶ E.obj.obj) (hu : IsEtale u) : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift (𝟙 (yoneda.obj U)) (𝟙 (yoneda.obj U)) (by simp) : yoneda.obj U ⟶ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback u u) ∧ ∀ (C : Over S) (c : yoneda.obj C ⟶ E.obj.obj), ∃ (W : Over S) (p : W ⟶ C) (q : yoneda.obj W ⟶ yoneda.obj U), IsPullback q (yoneda.map p) u c ∧ IsSeparated p.left
